1	# Agent Note: What the hypothesis program measured on the operator's subscription
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-08-hypothesis-program-results.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The hypothesis program ([slate](2026-09-07-hypothesis-program.md)) promised that every experiment would end with a verdict and an interval recorded under `data/proving-ground/`, and that a refutation would be recorded with the same care as a confirmation. Two days of runs on the operator's Claude Code subscription produced thirty records and eleven folds; nothing summarizes them, so a reader who wants to know whether the harness loop beats the product's own loop, whether a smaller model is worse, whether the directive loop earns its attempts, whether a knowledge pack changes anything, and what a router could gain has to read the proving-ground README end to end. This note is that summary, with the refutations first and the noise floor stated before any delta.
10	
11	## Proposal
12	
13	Read the records as follows, adopt the readings as the current state of knowledge about this harness on these tasks, and queue the slices the results demand rather than any change the results do not support.
14	
15	### The instrument, and what it can tell apart
16	
17	Every number below comes from a frozen paired experiment or a fleet run on `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/`: thirty zero-dependency program tasks in tiers 2 to 4 plus ten tier-5 tasks whose hidden cases the validator holds, eight of them audited so that every hidden case is derivable from the prompt. A cell is one task, one repetition, one arm; the runner validates the workspace against the task's checks after each attempt, issues a directive clustered by failing channel, and certifies when every case passes. Since 09:25 UTC on 2026-09-08 every cell is sealed: bubblewrap mounts an empty parent over the run directory with only the cell's workspace bound back in, the read barrier denies the parent and grants the workspace, and reads the barrier refuses are counted on the run. Two facts about the instrument bound every reading:
18	
19	- **The noise floor is one flip in sixteen.** The middle product model ran the same sixteen sealed tier-5 cells twice at seed 2 (the twentieth and twenty-first records); the runs agree on fifteen cells ([fold](../../../../data/proving-ground/folds/2026-09-08-sonnet-repeatability-t5-seed2.json)). Against an unsealed run of the same arm the agreement is fourteen and thirteen of sixteen, with one task (conf-canon) certified twice in both sealed runs and never in the unsealed one. A paired delta of 0.0625 on sixteen cells is inside one arm's own run-to-run variation; a delta has to be three flips wide before it says anything.
20	- **The arms of every recorded experiment ran one after the other, not interleaved.** The experiments service ran the whole baseline arm and then the whole candidate arm, so an arm of these records is confounded with its hour on the shared subscription. Seed pairing does not remove this. The cell-interleaved schedule is the slice below.
21	
22	### What was measured
23	
24	| Experiment | Tier, cells | Arms | Certified | Delta, interval, verdict | What separates the arms |
25	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26	| E2 harness loop vs product loop | 3, 36 | route vs delegated product, same model | 18 of 18 vs 18 of 18 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive | wall time level (harness faster in 11 of 18 pairs, medians 164 vs 179 s); harness spend write-dominant before session continuity (3,005,288 cache-write tokens over 200 queries) |
27	| E2 as two fleets | 2 and 4, 12 + 18 each | same | 30 of 30 vs 30 of 30 | fleets, not folded | harness faster on tier 2 (9 of 12 pairs), slower on tier 4 (6 of 18 pairs, 2,915 vs 2,292 s of cell time) |
28	| E2 on tier 5, unsealed | 5, 32 | same, audited tasks, seed 2 | 12 of 16 vs 11 of 16 | −0.0625, [−0.125, 0], inconclusive | inside the noise floor; the product arm ran uncapped and its misses cost up to 3,459 s and 5.60 USD each |
29	| E2 on tier 5, sealed, capped | 5, 32 | same, same caps on both arms, continuity | 15 of 16 vs 14 of 16 | −0.0625, [−0.125, 0], inconclusive | one flip, inside the noise floor; the product's two misses each breached a cap after one attempt; harness faster in 15 of 16 pairs (5,740 vs 8,187 s) and cheaper (7,695,132 vs 25,817,220 billed tokens) |
30	| E1 small vs middle | 3, 36 | sonnet vs haiku | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive | small model 405 steps vs 182, 6,719 vs 3,807 s, 844,538 vs 358,054 output tokens |
31	| E1 middle vs large | 3, 36 | sonnet vs opus | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive | large model 156 steps vs 208, 2,070 vs 3,948 s, 166,606 vs 367,172 output tokens |
32	| E1 middle vs large, sealed | 5, 32 | sonnet vs opus, seed 2 | 13 vs 16 | 0.1875, [0.125, 0.25], promote | large model first-attempt on every cell; 164 steps vs 267, 3,572 vs 7,451 s, 189,169 vs 561,271 output tokens |
33	| E1 small vs middle, sealed | 5, 32 | sonnet vs haiku, seed 2 | 14 vs 1 | −0.8125, [−0.875, −0.75], reject | small model spent all three attempts on fifteen cells; 604 steps vs 262, 11,227 vs 6,337 s, 736,856 vs 481,591 output tokens |
34	| E3 attempts, tier 3 | 3, 18 + 18 | three attempts vs one | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], fold says nothing | no cell used a second attempt |
35	| E3 attempts, tier 5 counterfactual | 5, 16 re-read | three vs one, from one run each | harness 11 vs 8; product 11 vs 11 | −0.1875, [−0.25, −0.125], reject for the cap; product 0 | the product loop's later attempts were a fresh child with the directive alone |
36	| E3 attempts, tier 5 paired | 5, 32 | three-rung vs one-rung ladder, same model | 15 of 16 vs 9 of 16 | −0.375, [−0.5625, −0.1875], reject for the cap of one | three certificates at a second attempt after a directive; the other three are first-attempt variation the loop absorbs (first attempts disagree on 9 of 16 cells between the arms); the later attempts cost 289 s and 39,158 output tokens over sixteen cells |
37	| E4 knowledge pack | 3, 18 + 18 | 2026-q3 pack mounted vs none | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], null | the pack was never opened: no skill call in any cell |
38	| E4 craft skills | 5, 16 folded against four sealed middle-model arms | three task-relevant skills mounted vs none | 13 of 16 vs 14, 13, 15, 15 of 16 | −0.0625, 0, −0.125, −0.125; every interval touches zero; inconclusive four times | every cell read all three skills; no certificate added, one task missed that no baseline missed; cache-write above every baseline |
39	| E5 downshift | 5, 32 | opus on three rungs vs opus then haiku, haiku, transcript kept | 16 vs 16 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive by construction | the largest model certified every cell at the first attempt in both arms, so the downshift rung never ran; two runs of one arm put the cost noise floor under 7 percent in output tokens and 15 percent in cell time |
40	| E5 handoff tax | 5, 32 | opus on three rungs vs haiku then opus, opus, transcript kept | 16 vs 14 | −0.125, [−0.25, 0], inconclusive | the ladder recovered 12 of the 14 certificates the smallest model missed and cost 2.5 times the strong model alone on every measure (8,122 vs 3,251 s, 500,664 vs 198,637 output tokens); the strong model's work after the handoff was no cheaper than its own first attempt, and it missed twice on tasks it never misses from a clean start |
41	| E5 drop | 5, 16 + 16 folded | haiku then opus, opus with the transcript kept (route) vs the same ladder with a fresh in-process child per rung (spawn), folded offline after the frozen pair lost its candidate arm | 11 of 16 vs 14 of 16 | 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], promote as an offline fold | three cells flipped, all toward the fresh child and all on the three hardest tasks, none the other way; both arms' first rungs certified 2 of 16; the fresh child cost more in total (575,350 vs 471,583 output tokens, 16.6 vs 14.9 million billed) and its two misses never reached the strong rung because the cheap rung alone spent the cell's token cap |
42	| Held-out estimate | 2 to 5, 16 | the middle model on the harness loop, one fleet, seed 3 | 15 of 16 | not an experiment | every certificate at the first attempt; the one miss is a tier-5 task after three attempts (3 of 4 on the two tier-5 tasks, 12 of 12 on tiers 2 and 3); the eight environments were untouched by the audit, the overlays, and the folds |
43	| Roles matrix | one run each | implementer, validator, judge, program, bridge | five roles work on the route | not an experiment | the two-turn bound broke every role until the native-tool route |
44	| Self-assessment | one program | one department on the route, committed verifier | released after operator intervention | not an experiment | uncommitted tree certified, unconfined integration, resume refused: the integrity slice |
45	
46	### What was refuted
47	
48	- **The harness loop loses to the product loop on the same model.** Refuted on tiers 2 to 4: 48 of 48 against 48 of 48, level wall time. On tier 5 the two loops are inside the noise floor of each other: 12 against 11 unsealed and uncapped, 15 against 14 sealed under the same caps, where the product loop's two misses each breached a cap after one attempt and the harness loop was faster in 15 of 16 pairs and cheaper by a factor of three in billed tokens. The harness loop is not better on certificates: what it adds is the record, the seal, and caps that hold.
49	- **A smaller model is as good on these tasks.** Refuted at tier 5, where the tier-3 reading that all three models are level (18 of 18 each) turns out to be saturation: the smallest model certifies 1 of 16, the middle 13 and 14, the largest 16 of 16, and the order is strict per cell. The tier-3 result stands only where the tasks do not separate; a bench that saturates cannot rank.
50	- **A cheap-first cascade saves money.** Refuted on the three single-model arms ([fold](../../../../data/proving-ground/folds/2026-09-08-routing-t5-seed2.json)): because the models order strictly per cell, the oracle that picks the cheapest certifying model is the largest model alone (16 of 16 at 189,169 output tokens and 3,572 s), the strong-first cascade is the same, and every cascade that starts lower pays the smaller model's whole failure first: middle-then-large costs 2.8 times the output tokens and 2.0 times the time, cheap-first over all three 6.6 and 5.0 times. On this bench the routing question is not which model to try first but whether a hard cell can be told apart before any model runs, and nothing in the stamp tells it apart.
51	- **Attempts do not matter.** Refuted on tier 5 for the harness loop, first by the counterfactual (three of eleven certificates came at the second attempt after a clustered directive, delta −0.1875 for a cap of one) and then by the frozen pair: a three-rung ladder against a one-rung ladder of the same model certified 15 against 9 of 16, delta −0.375, interval [−0.5625, −0.1875], reject for the cap, the first frozen verdict about a mechanism of the harness. Half of that delta is the later attempts themselves; the other half is first-attempt variation (the two arms' first attempts, which are the same delivery, disagree on nine of sixteen cells) that the loop absorbs, so a one-attempt reading of any model on this bench is a noisier instrument than the three-attempt one. Confirmed as null on tier 3, where no second attempt was taken.
52	- **Knowledge helps by being present.** Refuted from both sides. A catalog the tasks do not call for is never opened and costs wall time (5,433 s against 3,959) whose cause one fleet cannot assign. Three skills the tasks do call for are opened in every cell, all three, and add no certificate: 13 of 16 against 14, 13, 15, and 15 in the four sealed runs of the same model on the same cells, folds of −0.0625, 0, −0.125, and −0.125 that never rise above zero, one task missed that no baseline had missed, and the highest cache-write of the five runs. What the middle model misses on these tasks is not what a page of craft tells it.
53	
54	### What was supported
55	
56	- **The largest product model beats the middle one on tier 5.** The one promotion-level verdict from a frozen pair: 16 of 16 against 13, 0.1875, [0.125, 0.25], the largest model first-attempt on every cell and cheaper on every measure. It ranks a model tier, not the harness.
57	- **Dropping the cheap model's transcript at the hand-off beats keeping it.** 14 of 16 against 11 on the same ladder, 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], three flips all one way and all on the hardest tasks, as an offline fold of two arms run an hour apart on a shared subscription with sixteen cells each; the frozen pair on the fixed overlay is queued before anything is promoted on it.
58	
59	### What stayed inconclusive, and why
60	
61	Tiers 2 to 4 are saturated on certificates for all three product models under both loops, so every comparison there is inconclusive by construction and the information lives in steps, wall time, and spend. Tier 5 separates models completely and loops not at all; sixteen cells give an interval no narrower than ±0.19 for a real difference, and the noise floor is 0.0625. The bench can promote a model tier and it can refute; no frozen pair has promoted a harness change, the one harness mechanism with a promotion-level reading (the fresh child per rung) has it from an offline fold, and every harness change that landed this week (native tools, continuity, parity, the seal, the ladder) landed because a run showed a defect, not because an experiment showed a gain. The number to quote for the harness loop on the middle model is the held-out estimate: 15 of 16 with every certificate at the first attempt on eight environments nothing in the program had touched ([record](../../../../data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-bench-held-out-sonnet-all/manifest.json)), with the caveat that six of the eight are tier 2 or 3 and the two tier-5 tasks read 3 of 4.
62	
63	### Spend
64	
65	Before session continuity every harness-loop step on the route opened a fresh product session and rewrote its prefix: 4,778,361 cache-write tokens for sixteen tier-5 cells against 745,264 cache-read. With one product session resumed per harness session the spend is read-dominant: 2,185,841 cache-read against 317,394 cache-write for the large model's sixteen sealed cells, 8,515,603 against 738,281 for the middle model's. The product loop's spend was read-dominant from the start and its misses ran up to 3,459 s and 5.60 USD each until the budget-parity slice applied the cell's caps to a delegated attempt. The smallest model is the most expensive arm on record because a cell that fails three times rereads its growing transcript three times over: 21,275,855 cache-read tokens for sixteen cells.
66	
67	### Routing, E5, and what the ladder makes possible
68	
69	The attempt ladder lets an arm name a model per attempt and the transcript interface of the hand-off, and E5 ran on it as three readings. The downshift never happened: the largest model certified every cell at its first rung in both arms, so the cheap rung it was to hand down to never ran, and the experiment measures only the cost noise floor of one arm run twice. The handoff tax is real: the cheap-first ladder with the transcript kept recovered 12 of the 14 certificates the smallest model misses, cost 2.5 times the strong model alone, and lost two certificates the strong model never loses from a clean start. The drop reading is the one result in a harness mechanism's favour: the same ladder with a fresh in-process child per rung, so the strong model inherits the workspace and the directive but not the cheap model's transcript, certified 14 of 16 against 11 with the transcript kept, three flips all one way and all on the hardest tasks, 0.1875 with an interval of [0.0625, 0.3125]. It is an offline fold, because the frozen pair lost its candidate arm to a composition defect (the overlay patched an entry the base never names, which the include plugin skipped with a warning nothing printed) and its two arms ran an hour apart; it is evidence for the slate's prediction that dropping the cheap transcript beats keeping it, not a promotion, and the frozen pair is queued. Where the fresh child still missed, the cheap rung alone had spent the cell's token cap before the strong rung ran, which is a budget allocation defect of the ladder, not a transcript effect. On these cells raw escalation still cannot beat starting strong on cost, so what the ladder buys is a cheaper answer on the cells the cheap model can do (2 of 16 here) at a higher total cost on the rest. A per-turn router in the style of Fugu is not tested by any of this and is not proposed.
70	
71	## Slices the results demand
72	
73	- **Interleave the arms** ([note](../../implemented/architecture/2026-09-18-interleaved-experiment-arms.md)): the experiments service schedules cells pairwise (baseline then candidate of the same cell, alternating) so an arm is not confounded with its hour. The digest and the fold are unchanged.
74	- **Freeze the drop pair and share the cap per rung.** The drop comparison runs again as one frozen experiment on the fixed overlay, and each rung of a ladder gets its own share of the cell's token cap, so a cheap first rung cannot spend the strong rung's budget; the two misses of the drop arm were exactly that.
75	- **A harder tier or more cells before any harness promotion.** Sixteen cells cannot show a harness effect smaller than 0.19; the next paired harness experiment runs four repetitions or sixteen tasks, and the tier-5 tasks that every model certifies at the first attempt (five of eight for the middle model) do not discriminate.
76	- **Program workflow integrity** ([note](2026-09-08-program-workflow-integrity.md)): a department certifies only a committed tree, the integration runs confined, an interrupted integration resumes.
77	- **The process claim over the route**: the census attributes the route's own product spawn to the route so a route cell can claim `process` isolation (task 85).
78	
79	## Alternatives considered
80	
81	- **Report the certificate rates as a leaderboard.** Rejected: the observatory ranks only from experiment verdicts; the two promotion-level verdicts on record rank model tiers, and a leaderboard of the rest would rank noise.
82	- **Raise the repetitions until an interval excludes zero.** Rejected for the loop comparison: at two cells at a time a tier-5 experiment of 32 cells takes two and a half hours, and the reading that the two loops are level on tiers 2 to 4 would not change with more cells; the money goes to tier 5, the ladder, and a harder tier.
83	- **Import a public benchmark before drawing any conclusion.** Deferred as the slate says; the readings above are about this harness on this bench, and say so.
84	
85	## Acceptance criteria
86	
87	- Every row of the table above points at a record or fold under `data/proving-ground/` with sessions on disk.
88	- The results section of the slate note links here, and the observatory shows no ranking from these runs beyond the two model-tier verdicts.
89	- No row of the table is a placeholder: the sealed E2 rerun, the frozen E3 pair, the craft fold, the three E5 readings, and the held-out estimate each replaced theirs in the same change as their record.
90	
91	## Risks
92	
93	- Sixteen cells per arm on tier 5 is a small sample; the counterfactual intervals understate run-to-run variance and are labelled so; the noise floor above is measured from two runs, not twenty.
94	- The drop reading is an offline fold of two arms run an hour apart, and its candidate arm ran only after the frozen pair failed; its verdict label comes from the fold's own thresholds, and this note treats it as evidence.
95	- The arms ran sequentially on a shared subscription; a model-side change or load between the two arms would read as an arm effect.
96	- The tasks are authored in-house; the audit fixed three specification corners after both loops missed them, and a later audit may find more.
97	- The product envelope around every route query is model-visible and not in the log; both arms carry it, so comparisons hold and absolute costs include it.
98

1	# Agent Note: The implementer preflight a plan runs, and the include patch that must reach something
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-08-implementer-preflight-and-include-patch-gate.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A frozen paired experiment ran its entire baseline arm — 16 cells and about an hour of model budget — and then every cell of its candidate arm was refused by [`dsh-environment-runner`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/README.md) with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE`: `implementer provider "spawn" is unavailable: no subagent provider is registered under that name`.
10	
11	The provider was missing because the composition overlay never composed it. [`dsh-fleet`](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) keeps a cell whose run throws as a cell error, which is what makes one broken cell not fail a plan, so all 16 refusals were recorded as cell errors and the fleet run reported normally. The experiment then folded a comparison with `seedsPaired: 0` and a verdict of `inconclusive`. Nothing failed loudly anywhere: the only record that the candidate arm never ran is a per-cell error string in a report, and the shape of that report is the same one a genuinely inconclusive comparison produces.
12	
13	The refusal itself is correct and it is already early — `requireImplementer(implementer, model)` runs before any agent exists, checking that the named provider is composed, that this process can confine it under the deployment's isolation, that it can be told which model to run, and that a budget policy exists to bound it. It is private, so the only way to reach it is to start a cell. `ExperimentService.run()` documents that "Every refusal happens before the first cell runs"; for this refusal it was not true, and the cost of that is one arm of model spend per plan.
14	
15	The composition-side cause is a second silent skip. The overlay carried `- id: subagent-spawn` as a non-insert patch, and the base composition names no entry under that id. `applyEntryPatches` in [the vendored include plugin](../../../../vendor/include/src/index.ts) warns `patch: entry %C not found` and skips such a patch rather than refusing it, so the overlay mounted without the row it exists to add. The warning goes to the loader logger of a bench boot nobody reads. Two more checked-in compositions carry the same defect today: `examples/headless-agent/e2b.cordis.yml` patches `subprocess` and `fs-local` through `advanced.cordis.yml`, whose own entries are one nested include below, and the proving-ground `route-only` overlay patches a `tool-fs-search` row the bench base never composes.
16	
17	## Proposal
18	
19	**The runner publishes the preflight it already performs.** `EnvironmentRunner.checkImplementer(implementer, model)` takes one implementer and one stamped route, returns nothing, and throws the same `EnvironmentRunError` codes — `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE`, `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNCONFINED`, `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED`, `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNBOUNDED`. It calls the private `requireImplementer` and discards the resolved implementer, so there is one resolution and a caller cannot be told something `run()` would not enforce. A route implementer is refused nothing, because the session's own model route is what a run naming no implementer already uses.
20	
21	**The fleet refuses a plan before it mints a workspace.** `FleetService.run()` calls the preflight during plan validation, after the environment selection and the model default and before any cell is enumerated or any `mkdtemp` runs, once per route the plan names. The route it passes is the one the runner stamps: the plan's first ladder rung where that rung names a model, and the cell's own route otherwise. The runner's error propagates unchanged, so the plan is refused with the provider named instead of running as a plan of error cells.
22	
23	**The experiment refuses at freeze.** `ExperimentService.freeze()` runs the preflight for both arms, each against its own `{ provider, model }` route, in the per-arm validation loop that already refuses a conflicting first ladder rung, and before `agreedCaps` resolves the caps the digest freezes. Arms run in role order, so this is what keeps a candidate arm's missing provider from spending the baseline arm first.
24	
25	**An unmatched include patch fails a gate.** `verify-cordis-config` resolves each `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include` entry's `path` against the directory of the file the entry is written in, parses the included file as an entry list, and calls `applyEntryPatches` with a warning sink that collects instead of logging. Every collected warning becomes a gate error naming the file, the entry, and the included path. Calling the include's own function is what keeps the gate and the mount from disagreeing: ids match through group `config` lists, an `insert` adds ids a later patch in the same list may target, and the four skip conditions — an unmatched id, an insert into a row that is not a group, a patch carrying no id, and a `name` that disagrees with its target — are the plugin's, not a second implementation of them. An include whose file is absent uses its `initial` list, which is what the plugin writes there and reads back; an include naming a path that can be read as nothing else is an error too.
26	
27	The three compositions the gate rejects are fixed with it. The two proving-ground overlays gain `insert:` patches, which is what they meant. `e2b.cordis.yml` layers over `cordis.yml` directly and restates the rows `advanced.cordis.yml` adds, because the local `fs` and `subprocess` providers it must disable are only reachable in the file that declares them — and both of those services may be provided once per composition, so that overlay could not boot.
28	
29	## Alternatives considered
30	
31	**Let the fleet record the refusal as a plan-level error instead of forwarding the runner's.** A `FLEET_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE` would keep every refusal the fleet raises inside `FleetError`. It also restates four conditions the runner owns, and the message a planner reads would be the fleet's paraphrase of a provider fact the runner is authoritative about. Forwarding keeps one text and one code per condition.
32	
33	**Have the fleet resolve the plan's ladder through `resolveLadder` before checking.** The runner's resolution also validates rung count against the runner's own `maxLadderRungs`, which is deliberately a per-cell refusal rather than a plan-level one, so calling it here would move that ceiling to the plan. Reading `ladder[0].model` is the stamping rule alone, which is all the preflight needs.
34	
35	**Check the implementer once for the plan rather than once per route.** The current conditions do not read the route, so one call would raise the same errors. The runner's method answers for one stamped route, and every route a plan names is a route its cells would be stamped with; asking about each is what makes the plan's question the same question its cells ask.
36	
37	**Make the include throw on an unmatched patch instead of gating the files.** Refusing at mount is the loudest possible failure, and it changes the vendored plugin: patch lists compose one layer per source, and a layer that patches a row another layer may or may not insert is a supported use of the skip. The gate reads the checked-in composition, where every layer is known, so it can be strict without constraining the runtime.
38	
39	**Follow nested includes when building the id map.** It would make `e2b.cordis.yml` pass unchanged. It would also make the gate say a patch reaches an entry that at mount it does not, since `applyEntryPatches` recurses through group entries only. A gate that models something other than the mount is worse than no gate.
40	
41	## Acceptance criteria
42	
43	- `ctx.environmentRuns.checkImplementer` throws each of the four implementer codes for the composition that provokes it, creates no agent and starts no child, and returns for a composed in-process provider and for `{ kind: 'route' }`.
44	- A fleet plan naming a subagent provider the composition does not hold rejects with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE`, hands no cell to the runner, and leaves the plan's `workspaceRoot` empty. A plan whose provider is composed checks each route it names, and a laddered plan checks the first rung's model.
45	- An experiment whose candidate arm names such a provider rejects from `run()` with no `ctx.fleet.run` call at all, so the baseline arm runs no cell; a plan both of whose arms are honorable checks baseline then candidate, each against its own route.
46	- `verify-cordis-config` rejects a composition whose include entry carries a non-insert patch matching no entry of the included file, and accepts patches that reach an entry directly, inside a group, and through a row an earlier `insert` in the same list added. The gate passes over every checked-in composition.
47	
48	## Risks
49	
50	- **The preflight is a snapshot of the composition, not a reservation.** Nothing keeps a provider registered between the plan check and the last cell, so a provider disposed mid-run still fails its cells the way it does today. The check removes the case where the plan could never have run, not the case where it stopped being able to.
51	- **A plan-level refusal replaces a partial result with none.** A driver that could previously read a fleet report whose cells all failed now gets a thrown error and no report. That is the intent for an implementer the composition cannot honor, and it is a behavior change for any consumer that treated the all-errors report as a normal outcome.
52	- **The include gate is as strict as the compositions are honest.** It reads the file each include entry names, so a composition assembled at runtime from a path this gate cannot resolve is still unchecked, and a patch list whose target file is generated during a boot passes on its `initial` list rather than the file that will exist. Both are outside what a checked-in composition states.
53

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Run one with `pnpm run bench -- fleet <name>` (a `models` array) or `pnpm run bench -- experiment <name>` (a `baseline`/`candidate` pair); `pnpm run bench -- plans` prints this same information parsed live from each file. 271:The thirtieth record is the drop arm run as a fleet under the fixed overlay, launched at 17:43 UTC, eighty minutes after its baseline: the same 16 cells, seed 2, the same ladder, every rung a fresh in-process child of the runner's process on the rung's model with the task restated and the directive carried, the same caps, 5,816 s of wall time at two cells at a time. It certified 14 of 16: 2 at the first rung by the smallest model (ranked-choice, both repetitions), 11 at the second rung by the largest, and 1 at the third (diff3-merge); its two misses (conf-canon and sheet-eval, one repetition each) never reached the strong rung, because the smallest model's single attempt had spent 1,493,040 and 1,472,984 of the cell's 1,500,000 billed tokens rereading its own transcript, and the runner refused the second rung on the breached cap. Folded offline against the twenty-ninth's baseline arm ([folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json)), the reading is 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], `promote` by the fold's thresholds: three cells flipped, all toward the fresh child and all on the three tasks the kept transcript failed (build-schedule, conf-canon, sheet-eval), none the other way, with both arms' first rungs at 2 of 16. The fresh child is not cheaper: 575,350 output tokens against 471,583, 16,648,949 billed against 14,911,342, 11,377 s of cell time (median 678 s) against 6,964 (median 441), because every rung reads the task and the workspace from nothing; what it buys is a strong rung that starts from the workspace and the directive instead of from the cheap model's transcript. The fold is offline: its arms ran an hour apart on the shared subscription and were not frozen together, so it is evidence for the slate's prediction that dropping the cheap transcript beats keeping it, not a promotion; the frozen pair on the fixed overlay and a per-rung share of the token cap are queued. The usage of a delegated cell is summed over its `environment/delegation` events, which carry each child's reported model and usage; the census finds no cell leaving its workspace and no read denied.
273:The twenty-ninth record is the drop arm of the routing hypothesis as it first ran, a frozen paired experiment whose candidate arm never started: the baseline arm, the smallest model on the first rung and the largest on the second and third with the transcript kept (the twenty-seventh's ladder again, on the route), ran its 16 sealed tier-5 cells at seed 2 in 3,760 s of wall time at two cells at a time and certified 11 of 16, 2 at the first rung and 9 at the second, its five misses each stopped by the 1,500,000 billed-token cap (1,471,243 to 1,515,456 billed tokens); the candidate arm, the same ladder with every rung a fresh in-process child through the spawn provider, was refused at every cell before a session existed, because [overlays/with-spawn.cordis.yml](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/overlays/with-spawn.cordis.yml) patched an entry the base composition never names and the include plugin skips such a patch with a warning nothing printed, so no provider was registered under `spawn`. The experiment folded to `inconclusive` with no seed paired ([result.json](2026-09-08-bench-e5-handoff-drop-t5/result.json)), an hour of the largest model spent before a misconfiguration the composition could have refused at load: the overlay now inserts the provider (`5e06f652d`), the fleet and the experiments service refuse an unavailable implementer before any cell runs, and `verify-cordis-config` fails on an include patch that reaches nothing (`f0a684ef0`), which found two more compositions with the same defect. The census finds four cells leaving their workspace in eight tool calls, two of them naming the run directory, and no read denied.
277:The twenty-seventh record is the handoff tax as a frozen paired experiment on the attempt ladder: the largest product model on three rungs as the baseline against the smallest model on the first rung and the largest on the second and third with the transcript kept, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,862 s of wall time at two cells at a time, sealed. The baseline certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt, the fourth such sweep of the largest model on these cells. The ladder certified 14 of 16: the smallest model's first attempt made 2 (lex-states and ranked-choice, one repetition each), the largest model on the second rung recovered 11, the third rung 1 more (diff3-merge), and two cells ran all three attempts out (conf-canon and rate-limit-sim, one repetition each), where the largest model, holding a failed first attempt it did not write, missed twice on tasks it has never missed from a clean start in 64 cells. Delta −0.125, interval [−0.25, 0], inconclusive: two cells in sixteen, at the noise floor, and never above zero. The tax is in the cost, not the verdict. The ladder spent 8,122 s of cell time against 3,251 (medians 531 s against 175), 535 model steps against 181, 500,664 output tokens against 198,637, 1,150,560 cache-write against 328,456, and 14,245,694 cache-read against 2,651,444; the smallest model's rung alone cost 406 steps, 312,430 output tokens, and 9,401,938 cache-read before the largest model ran at all, and the largest model's own share after the handoff (129 steps, 188,234 output tokens) is within a step or a token of what it spends from a clean start (181 and 198,637 here, 164 and 189,169 in the twentieth record), so the inherited transcript saved it nothing. Escalating from the cheap model to the strong one on these tasks recovers most of the certificates the cheap model misses, 12 of 14, and costs two and a half times what starting strong costs on every measure while giving back two certificates. The offline cascade of the twenty-first record priced this order at 4.9 times the largest model's output tokens because it charged the smallest model's whole three-attempt failure before escalating; the ladder escalates after one attempt and pays 2.5 times, so the live reading is cheaper than the offline one and the conclusion is the same, since the strong model's work after the handoff is no cheaper than its own first attempt. The census finds six cells leaving their workspace in eight tool calls, two naming the run directory or a sibling, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied.
279:The twenty-sixth record is the downshift arm of the routing hypothesis as a frozen paired experiment on the attempt ladder: the largest product model on three rungs as the baseline against the largest model on the first rung and the smallest on the second and third with the transcript kept, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 3,192 s of wall time at two cells at a time, sealed. The downshift never happened: the largest model certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt in both arms, so no cell reached a rung the smallest model would have run, the two arms are two runs of the same thing, and the fold reads 0, [0, 0], inconclusive by construction. The record is still worth its cells for two readings. It is the second and third first-attempt sweep of the largest model on these cells after the twentieth record (and the baseline arm of the twenty-seventh, running as this is written, is a fourth), so the top of the model order is as repeatable as the middle model's flips are not. And two runs of one arm give the cost noise floor the way three runs of the middle model gave the certificate noise floor: 174,804 against 186,731 output tokens, 291,756 against 307,765 cache-write, 1,894,101 against 2,240,677 cache-read, 146 against 157 model steps, 2,903 against 3,328 s of cell time with the same 156 s median, so a spend difference under 7 percent in output tokens or 15 percent in cell time between two arms of one model is within one arm's own variation. The downshift question, whether the cheap model can finish what the strong one started, cannot be posed on a bench the strong model finishes alone at the first attempt; it needs tasks the largest model itself takes a second attempt on, which no admitted tier holds. The census finds three cells leaving their workspace in four tool calls, none naming the run directory or a sibling, and no read denied.
285:The twenty-third record is the attempt hypothesis as one frozen paired experiment, which the attempt ladder made possible: the runner takes a ladder's length as a run's attempt bound, so the baseline arm ladders three rungs of the middle model and the candidate one rung of the same model on the same route, and the two arms differ in exactly the cap, with no overlay and no offline fold. Over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,666 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with continuity, the three-attempt arm certified 15 of 16 (12 at the first attempt, build-schedule, diff3-merge, and lex-states once each at the second, sheet-eval missed once after three) and the one-attempt arm 9 of 16, delta −0.375, interval [−0.5625, −0.1875], verdict reject for the cap of one: the interval clears the 0.0625 noise floor six times over, and it is the first frozen verdict on record about a mechanism of the harness rather than a model. Read the difference in two parts. Three of the sixteen certificates came at a second attempt after a clustered directive, which is the −0.1875 the counterfactual fold of the eleventh record predicted and exactly what a cap of one forfeits. The other three come from the first attempts themselves: the one-attempt arm's first attempts certified 9 of 16 where the three-attempt arm's certified 12, and the first attempt is the same delivery under either ladder (the task statement alone, nothing about the cap reaches the model), so that part is run-to-run variation of first attempts, not an effect of the cap. Cell by cell the two arms' first attempts disagree on nine of sixteen (three the baseline missed and the candidate made, six the other way), while the final outcomes of two three-attempt runs of this arm disagree on one or two; the loop's value is that it absorbs first-attempt variance the tasks produce whatever the cap, and a single-attempt reading of any model on this bench is a noisier instrument than the three-attempt one by that margin. The cap did not buy speed: 5,689 s of cell time against 5,400 (medians 295 s against 300), 240 model steps against 219, 441,504 output tokens against 402,346, so the two later attempts cost 289 s and 39,158 output tokens over sixteen cells for six more certificates. The census finds eight cells naming their parent or the run directory in twelve tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied.
291:The twentieth record is the first frozen paired experiment on the sealed bench and the first whose interval excludes zero: the middle product model as the baseline arm against the largest as the candidate, on the harness loop, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,742 s of wall time at two cells at a time, under the composition that confines every cell with bwrap (a cell's parent directory is an empty tmpfs holding only the cell), resumes one product session per harness session, and forwards each hidden case's arguments through the reserved check script. The largest model certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt; the middle one 13 of 16 (11 at the first attempt, diff3-merge and rate-limit-sim once each at the second, sheet-eval missed twice at the 1,200,000 ms wall cap and lex-states once after three attempts), delta 0.1875, interval [0.125, 0.25], verdict promote at the 0.05 minimum delta: on these tasks the largest model is the better implementer, and the difference sits where the specification has corners the middle model does not reach in three attempts. The largest model was also the cheaper and faster arm on every measure: 164 model steps against 267, 3,572 s of cell time against 7,451 (median 204 s against 387), 189,169 output tokens against 561,271, and with session continuity now on the route the spend is read-dominant, 2,185,841 cache-read against 317,394 cache-write tokens for the candidate and 8,515,603 against 738,281 for the baseline, where the eighteenth record's harness loop wrote 2,927,150 and read 626,621. The census finds seven cells that named the run directory or their parent in eight tool calls; under the seal every such call saw an empty directory holding only the cell's own workspace, as the recorded results show, and no read was denied because nothing reachable was denied. This is the first promotion-level verdict of the program and it promotes a model, not a change to the harness; read with the thirteenth and fourteenth records it says the model tiers separate on certificates at tier 5 where tier 3 saturated, and it says nothing yet about the harness loop against the product loop, whose sealed rerun follows.
293:The nineteenth record is the harness assessing itself through its own program workflow: one department on the route, the largest product model, reading an eleven-file evidence dossier in its worktree (this README, the census, the record index, the last thirty hours of commits, the slate, the roles matrix, the sealed-cell note, the ruflo and baselines comparisons, and the question with the four goals) and writing `assessment.md`, certified by a committed verifier that requires four named sections, two verdict lines, at least eight evidence bullets each citing a dossier file that exists, six distinct files, and 600 to 2,500 words; the integration re-ran the verifier on the merged head. The department certified at its first validation after eleven steps (14 evidence bullets, 9 files cited, 2,258 words) with `Viable: undetermined (medium confidence)` and `State of the art: in part (medium confidence)`, the part being the measurement instrument and its enforcement rather than any measured capability; it also found that this lab's own summary table carries no contamination column and that the tier 2 to 4 comparisons are folds of separate fleets, not frozen experiments. The run exposed three defects in the program workflow, all kept in the artefacts directory beside the record ([2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json](2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json)): the department certified with the file written but never committed, so the integration merged an empty branch and failed on `missing assessment.md`; the integration agent, unconfined, then found the department's worktree and rewrote sentences of the certified file with a script before the operator stopped it after 22 steps; and the resume refused to republish the integration session's identity, so the operator committed the department tree as it then stood, set the first integration session aside, and resumed, after which the integration certified the merged head and the program released. The text the department certified is reconstructed byte for byte from its own session's write (`assessment.certified.md`, 2,258 words) and differs from the merged text in five lines, none of them a verdict.
295:The eighteenth record is the fourth frozen paired experiment and the tier-5 form of the eighth: the harness loop as the baseline arm against the product loop as the candidate arm, the same product model on both sides, on the eight tier-5 environments as audited (the conf-canon reference and six of its cases regenerated, the lex-states and sheet-eval prompts clarified), seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 8,979 s of wall time at two cells at a time. The harness loop certified 12 of 16 (9 at the first attempt, 3 at the second: diff3-merge, lex-states, and rate-limit-sim once each), the product loop 11 of 16 (10 at the first attempt and rate-limit-sim once at the second, the first recovery by a fresh child that received the directive alone), delta −0.0625, interval [−0.125, 0], verdict inconclusive. Three cells flip between the arms: the product loop certified conf-canon once where the harness loop never did, and the harness loop certified uri-resolve twice where the product loop's two cells failed three delegations each in 125 s with no reported model or cost, because they ran last, after 04:10 UTC, when the subscription's session limit had been reached (it reset at 05:30); on the 14 pairs the limit did not touch, the arms differ by one certificate in the product loop's favour. Both arms miss sheet-eval twice, the harness loop cut at the 1,200,000 ms wall cap and the product loop uncapped at 662 and 714 s, because in this run the composition's caps bound only the harness's own steps (the budget-parity slice landed after it). The product loop was the faster implementer, faster in 10 of 16 pairs, 7,554 s of cell time against 10,221, and reported 629,483 output tokens and 13.23 USD of list-price cost; the harness loop's 16 cells spent 802,872 output tokens, 626,621 cache-read and 2,927,150 cache-write tokens, with one transient route retry on each conf-canon cell that recovered. This record also carries the defect a census found after it: five of the harness loop's sixteen cells left their workspace for the run directory, read its plan and log and a sibling cell of their own environment (lex-states, rate-limit-sim, and conf-canon of the second repetition, and both sheet-eval cells), and the first sheet-eval cell did its work inside the second's workspace, while no product-loop cell left its own; the sealed-cell slice that denies a cell everything above its workspace is queued, and the tier-5 comparison is rerun under it before this verdict is read as more than what it is. Read with the eleventh and twelfth records, tier 5 does not separate the two loops on certificates either: both land at 11 or 12 of 16 on the same environments, with the misses on the same two tasks.
303:The fourteenth record is the third frozen paired experiment, the largest product model as the candidate arm against the middle one, on the same nine tier-3 environments and the harness loop: 36 cells, 3,024 s of wall time. Both arms certified 18 of 18, so the verdict is inconclusive on certificates for the third time on this tier, and the baseline arm needed a second attempt on two cells this time where its earlier runs needed none, which is the run-to-run variance a paired design absorbs. The largest model was the cheaper implementer on every other measure: 156 model steps against 208, 2,070 s of cell time against 3,948 (median 118 s against 165), 166,606 output tokens against 367,172, and 2,071,448 cache-write tokens against 3,635,010. Across the thirteenth and fourteenth records the three product models order by spend, not by certificates: the largest spends the least on the harness loop because it takes the fewest steps, and every step of this route rewrites the prefix.
305:The thirteenth record is the second frozen paired experiment, the model-tier comparison on the harness loop: the same nine tier-3 environments, two repetitions, the smaller product model as the candidate arm against the middle one as the baseline, 36 cells, 5,437 s of wall time. Both arms certified 18 of 18 at the first attempt, so the delta is again 0 with interval [0, 0] and the verdict inconclusive: on certificates at this tier the smaller model is not worse. Everything else separates the tiers: the smaller model needed 405 model steps against 182, 6,719 s of cell time against 3,807 (its median cell 300 s against 207), 844,538 output tokens against 358,054, and 9,985,537 cache-write tokens against 3,070,990. Read with the eighth record, the bench's tier 3 is saturated on certificates for all three of these product models under both loops, and the differences between models and between loops live in steps, wall time, and spend.
313:The ninth record is the harness loop's fleet over the same six tier-2 environments the fourth record measured with the product loop: twelve cells, every one certified in one attempt, 37 to 481 s per cell, median 116 s, 979 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 7.6 model steps per cell on average, 158,899 output tokens, 255,502 cache-read and 884,168 cache-write tokens. Set beside the fourth record cell by cell (the same environment and repetition, in different fleets rather than one frozen plan), the harness loop was faster in 9 of 12 pairs and its cells took 1786 s in total against the product loop's 1932 s.
315:The eighth record is the first frozen paired experiment of the hypothesis program (digest `4c9659e3…`): the harness's own loop on the Claude Code route as the baseline arm against the product's own loop as the candidate arm, the same model on both sides, over the nine tier-3 environments that are not held out, two repetitions, seed 1, 36 cells, 4194 s of wall time at two cells at a time. Both arms certified 18 of 18 cells at one attempt each, so the certificate-rate delta is 0 with a bootstrap interval of [0, 0] and the verdict is inconclusive at the 0.05 minimum delta: on this tier the harness loop is neither better nor worse than the product loop on certificates, which refutes the hypothesis that the harness loop loses to the product loop on these tasks and does not support the hypothesis that it wins. Wall time is also level: the harness loop was faster in 11 of the 18 pairs, its median cell took 164 s against 179 s, and the two arms' totals differ by under one percent. The harness loop's spend is on record because its queries go through the harness: 352,494 output tokens and 553,676 cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3,005,288 cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session whose prefix is written to the cache again instead of read from it; the product loop keeps one session per cell and pays that once. The product arm's spend is not on this record: the slice that forwards the cell's model to the child and records the child's reported usage and cost merged after the run had started (the manifest's head carries it, the runs do not), so the next paired experiment carries both arms' spend.
325:The third record is the same district left running overnight: 22 slots on its thirty-minute cadence from 22:16 to 09:16 UTC, including the first slot the second record holds. The host restarted once; the slot due at 00:16 was not caught up, exactly as the shift driver's cadence rule states, and the relaunched process resumed the same ledger and cadence from 00:46 on the working tree of that moment, so the slots before the restart ran the tree at `88f6a1f2e` and the slots after it the tree at `38dd04165`, which the manifest records as the head. Every one of the 66 cells was certified in one attempt; the record holds all 22 shift ledgers, the 66 cell sessions, and the exports folded over them.

Both product misses breached a cap after one attempt; the harness loop was faster in 15 of 16 pairs (5,740 s against 8,187) and 3.4 times cheaper in billed tokens. 387	  ['refuted', 'A smaller model is as good on these tasks.', 'At tier 5 the three product models order strictly on every cell: haiku certifies 1 of 16, sonnet 13 and 14, opus 16 of 16. 388	  ['refuted', 'A cheap-first cascade saves money.', 'Because the models order strictly per cell, the offline routing fold over the three single-model arms is exact. 389	  ['refuted', 'Attempts do not matter.', 'A three-rung ladder against a one-rung ladder of the same model on the same route, differing in exactly the cap: 15 of 16 against 9, delta −0.375, interval [−0.5625, −0.1875], reject for the cap of one. 390	  ['refuted', 'Knowledge helps by being present.', 'Refuted from both sides. 391	  ['supported', 'opus beats sonnet at tier 5.', 'The one promotion-level verdict from a frozen pair: 16 of 16 against 13, delta 0.1875, interval [0.125, 0.25], promote, with opus first-attempt on every cell and cheaper on every measure. 392	  ['supported', 'Dropping the cheap model’s transcript at the hand-off beats keeping it.', 'The same ladder with a fresh in-process child per rung, so the strong model inherits the workspace and the directive but not the cheap model’s transcript: 14 of 16 against 11, 0.1875, interval [0.0625, 0.3125], three flips all one way and all on the three hardest tasks. 393	  ['inconclusive', 'The downshift never happened.', 'opus on three rungs against opus then haiku, haiku with the transcript kept: 16 of 16 in both arms, 0, [0, 0], inconclusive by construction, because opus certified every cell at its first rung and the cheap rung never ran. 394	  ['inconclusive', 'The handoff tax is in the cost, not the verdict.', 'opus on three rungs against haiku then opus, opus with the transcript kept: 16 of 16 against 14, delta −0.125, interval [−0.25, 0], inconclusive. 395	  ['estimate', 'Held-out reliability: 15 of 16.', 'sonnet on the harness loop over the eight held-out environments (tiers 2 to 5, seed 3, two repetitions), untouched by the audit, the overlays and the folds: 15 of 16, every certificate at the first attempt, 3 of 4 on the two tier-5 tasks and 12 of 12 on tiers 2 and 3. # 2026-09-18-proving-ground-v1

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Every recorded Proving Ground trajectory folded into one file a trainer reads: the 750 trajectories the 29 records under [`data/proving-ground/`](../../README.md) carry, filtered to the 521 that measure the harness's own model route. [`tools/build-dataset.mjs`](../../tools/build-dataset.mjs) writes it from those records and nothing else; the records themselves are never edited, and nothing in this directory is written by hand.

## Files

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `train.jsonl` | 521 trajectories, ordered by record name then trajectory id |
| `heldout.jsonl` | The held-out environments' trajectories in the same format; always written, and empty unless the build is given `--include-held-out` |
| `manifest.json` | Name, build time, repository head, tool version, every source record with its manifest digest, the counts, the distributions of the written set, the token totals, and each written file's SHA-256 |

The two JSONL files are larger than this repository commits, so only `manifest.json` and this README pair are checked in; rebuild the rest with the command below and compare against the digests the manifest records. `train.jsonl` is 41 222 996 bytes at `f357ef8939b8a3296749d06969ab02aaf9db977ea0fc9bdea0af15c48aea3826`, and `heldout.jsonl` is empty, at the SHA-256 of no bytes.

Each line is the `dsh-trajectory/1` record [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) exported — `id`, `source`, `environment`, `config`, `system`, `tools`, `messages`, `steps`, `reward`, `parity`, `provenance` — with one field added:

```json
{ "dataset": { "record": "2026-09-08-bench-h1-harness-loop-t5", "tier": 5, "domain": "parsing", "arm": "fleet", "reward": { "value": 1, "basis": "certificate" } } }
```

`tier` and `domain` come from the environment's `task.json` under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/environments/`; an environment absent from that catalog — a smoke task, a live-district task, or a session no runner stamped — gets `null` for both, which in this build is the 106 unstamped sessions. `arm` is the stamp group's role suffix (`baseline`, `candidate`), `fleet` for a fleet batch, and `-` for a session in no group.

## Reward

`reward.value` is the exported `reward.outcome` and `reward.basis` says what decided it. A certificate is the only basis that can carry a positive value: the verifier ran the standard the runner authored before the work started, and `1` means a certificate covers the current standard revision. The same basis carries `0` for a goal that had a standard and never earned one — a measured failure. `none` means the log holds no goal, so nothing was measured and the value is `null`. `tamper` means the last recorded run found the check-owned files changed, which voids the measurement whatever else the log says; such a trajectory never reaches either file.

This corpus carries two of the four bases: 367 rows at `1` and 48 at `0`, both on a certificate, and 106 at `null` on `none`. The 106 unmeasured rows are the sessions no runner stamped — 77 shift-ledger sessions with no model turn at all, and 29 child sessions that cells of the `2026-09-08-bench-e5-drop-candidate-t5` fleet spawned, each naming its parent in `source.parentSession` and carrying its own turns under no stamp. No row carries `tamper` or `uncertified-completion`.

=== claude-code bundle README ===
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-claude-code`

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The dsh Claude Code bundle. [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) is a patch layer over [`dsh-base`](../base/README.md) and [`dsh-headless`](../headless/README.md) that serves every model request of the one-shot task mode from the Claude Code installation the operator has already authenticated, so `dsh --profile claude-code "task"` runs the same task mode as `--profile headless` without an API key. The package has no runtime API; the profile composer resolves the patch through the `dsh.bundle.patch` manifest field, never through code.

The layer reaches exactly three rows. It inserts `llm-claude-code` ([`dsh-llm-claude-code`](../../llm/llm-claude-code/README.md)) as the `claude-code` provider route over three models — `opus`, `sonnet`, and `haiku`, each carrying the `productModel` the installation is asked to run and a 200,000-token `contextWindow` — at `effort: medium` and a five-minute `queryTimeoutMs`. It repoints [`agent-default-model`](../../core/agent-default-model/README.md) at `claude-code`/`sonnet`; an id-targeted patch replaces the whole config, so both fields are restated. And it restates the `system-prompt` persona, because the headless persona renders `{{model}}` with nothing naming what serves it, and on this route that placeholder resolves to a product alias. Nothing else moves: the route injects `subprocess`, which the base layer already mounts as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local`, and the one-shot runner, its startup provider, and the disabled HMR row stay as `dsh-headless` composed them.

The keyed adapters stay mounted. [`llm-deepseek`](../../llm/llm-deepseek/README.md) resolves its credential per request and keeps its route registered and its catalog browsable without one, and [`llm-pi-ai`](../../llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md) registers no route at all until a `llm-pi-ai:` settings section supplies provider profiles. Neither fails a keyless load, so disabling them would only take away routes a user's own profile patch layer can still select.

## Model Experience

### The deployment persona

#### What the model sees

The persona this layer configures on the `system-prompt` row, rendered as the order-0 `deployment:persona` section, with `{{model}}` resolving to the selected model id — `sonnet` unless a request names another — and `{{cwd}}` to the session's working directory. Selecting the `claude-code` route also means that whole prompt reaches the model inside the installation's own system-prompt envelope, which [`dsh-llm-claude-code`](../../llm/llm-claude-code/README.md) neither authors nor can inspect.

##### Verbatim persona

```markdown
You are a coding agent powered by the Claude Code {{model}} model. Your working directory is {{cwd}}.
```

#### Token effect

One short sentence per request, replacing the persona `dsh-headless` configures rather than adding to it; the installation's envelope adds a further fixed amount this layer does not measure.

#### KV Cache effect

The persona sits at the head of the system prompt and is constant for a session, so it preserves the reusable prefix; under the route's default `per-session` continuity the installation reads that prefix back from its own prompt cache.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- **The installation's system-prompt envelope is not in the session log** — the harness authors the persona and every other prompt section, but the product wraps them in text this composition neither writes nor sees, so one model-visible input of every request cannot be reconstructed from the log.
- **One product session per harness session** — the route's default `per-session` continuity resumes a single product session across the steps of a run, so a process killed between steps leaves that session's transcript behind in the operator's own configuration directory.
- **The model ids are product aliases** — `opus`, `sonnet`, and `haiku` name what the installation is asked to run, not a pinned model version, so what a run executes changes with the installation rather than with this composition.

=== fleet README runPaired ===
42:`ctx.fleet.runPaired(first, second)` runs two plans as one batch and returns one report per plan, in the order the plans were given. Both plans are validated exactly as `run` validates one, and the pair itself is refused with `FLEET_INVALID_PLAN` when the two plans select different environments or ask for different repetitions — before either plan runs a cell, so a pair is never half spent. The batch runs environment-major, then repetition, then plan, so the two plans' cells of one environment and one repetition are adjacent, and both plans draw on the one `maxConcurrent` pool: at `maxConcurrent: 2` the two cells of a pair run at the same time. That is what keeps a plan from being confounded with the hour it ran in, which two `run` calls in a row cannot avoid. Each plan keeps its own group, district, ledger, and workspace retention, so each report — its group, its cells in its own plan order, its leaderboard, its spend — its `fleet/cell` events, its route breaker, and its token ceiling are what that plan's own `run` produces.
46:`policyVersion` names the checkpoint or policy the plan's routes serve; every cell's run stamp carries it verbatim, so a fold can key measured difficulty by it. `seed` is the plan's **base** seed and each cell runs with `seed + repetition`, so one repetition index means one seed across every route and every environment of the plan — which is what lets a paired design compare like with like. The base is validated once, at the plan boundary, because the arithmetic is the fleet's: a base the runner would refuse must not surface as every cell failing separately. A seed records what a run asked for, never what a provider did with it; the [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#sampling-and-what-a-replay-reproduces) owns what a replay can and cannot reproduce.
64:Right after a cell's outcome is recorded and its retention has run, the fleet emits the observe-only Cordis event `fleet/cell` with the plan's `group`, its `district` when it has one, the `cell`, and an `outcome` of `reported` with the runner's `sessionId` and `certified` flag or `error` with the failing code and message. One event per cell, in settle order — which equals plan order only while `maxConcurrent` is `1`, and which alternates between the two plans of a paired run, each event carrying its own plan's group and district. A listener cannot change the outcome and its failure is contained, so an observer such as [the shift driver](../shifts/README.md) writes its own per-cell record without holding this report; the [Cordis catalog](../../../docs/subsystems/improvement.md#cordis-surface) carries the declaration.
76:- **The leaderboard is a fold of one fleet run** — cross-run comparison, paired designs across variants, and confidence intervals read the `environment/run` stamps and certificates from the session logs; this package folds only the reports it just produced.

=== experiments README ===
5:A frozen, paired, budgeted comparison of two arms. A plan names the environments, the repetition count, and the two arms — each a model route and who implements its cells; a content digest freezes it before any cell runs; both arms run through `ctx.fleet` at the same repetition indexes under stamp groups derived from that digest; and the paired certificate-rate delta comes back with a bootstrap confidence interval, the caps both arms ran under, and a `promote` / `reject` / `inconclusive` verdict. Nothing here calls a model. The [experiments](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-experiments.md) and [budget-parity](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-08-budget-parity-for-delegated-cells.md) Agent Notes own the design rationale.
46:Both arms' implementers are checked at freeze, through `ctx.environmentRuns.checkImplementer` against each arm's own route, and the runner's `EnvironmentRunError` propagates unchanged. It is what keeps "every refusal happens before the first cell runs" true of a provider the composition cannot honor: the arms run as one batch, so a candidate arm whose provider is missing would otherwise spend the baseline arm's cells beside its own failing ones and then leave every repetition unpaired for a verdict of `inconclusive`.
52:Both arms are forwarded the same `policyVersion` and the same base `seed`, and each arm's cell samples with `seed + repetition`, so the paired repetitions of the two arms differ only in the arm itself, its route and its implementer — the [fleet README](../fleet/README.md#policy-version-and-the-base-seed) owns the arithmetic and the [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#sampling-and-what-a-replay-reproduces) what a replay reproduces.
54:Both arms then run as one `ctx.fleet.runPaired` call over the same ids at the same repetition count, each carrying its own arm's route and implementer. The fleet interleaves the two arms' cells — the baseline cell of one environment and repetition beside the candidate cell of the same one, then the next repetition, then the next environment — so an arm is not confounded with the hour it ran in, a provider-side drift between the arms lands on both, and each arm still comes back as the report its own plan would have produced alone. A cell the fleet kept as an error leaves its repetition unpaired rather than failing the experiment, and the result lists it under `errors` with its arm, environment, repetition, and the fleet's code and message, so a stored result says why a repetition did not pair without the process that ran it. The result is written to `sink` as one JSON line and the sink is closed exactly once; the sink is the trajectory exporter's `TrajectorySink`, so `jsonlFileSink(path)` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories` serves both exports.
74:A repetition pairs when both arms reported it. Per environment the result states `pairs`, `unpaired`, the `baselineRate` and `candidateRate` over the paired repetitions, their `delta`, the mean `attemptsDelta`, and the summed `inputTokenDelta` and `outputTokenDelta`; the overall `delta` is the mean over every paired repetition of every environment.
76:Each interval is a percentile bootstrap over the paired deltas: a resample draws, within every environment, as many paired deltas as that environment holds, with replacement, and the overall statistic of a resample is the mean over every drawn delta, so an environment weighs by its paired count and an environment with no pair contributes nothing rather than a zero. Every draw comes from a mulberry32 generator seeded with the 32-bit FNV-1a hash of `<digest>:<environmentId>`, so the same frozen plan over the same certificates replays to the same interval in any process; a fold with no pair at all reports no interval.
78:The verdict reads the overall interval: `promote` when its lower bound exceeds `minimumDelta`, `reject` when its upper bound is below zero, `inconclusive` otherwise — including when nothing paired. `promote` is tested first, so a negative `minimumDelta` still promotes rather than producing an order-dependent answer.
92:- **Paired repetition indexes are not paired seeds** — the `environment/run` stamp carries no seed, so pairing removes environment variance but not run-to-run variance.

=== runner README share ===
32:| `isolation` (required) | `none`, `process`, or `host`: the isolation the deployment can defend for its check runs. A local composition that shares the filesystem between implementer and validator is `none`; a run whose checks and fixtures live on another account or host is `host`. Written into every certificate and stamp; nothing in-process can verify it. |
57:A rung may also claim `share`, the fraction of every cap the cell runs under — tokens, wall clock, and cost — its attempt may consume before it is ended and the run moves to the next rung. The share is measured from the cell's caps rather than from what is left of them, so a cheap first rung cannot spend the budget a later rung was given; `[{ share: 0.3 }, {}]` gives the first attempt three tenths of the cell and leaves the rest to the second. A rung claiming none runs until the cell's own caps end it, which ends the cell with it. `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_LADDER` also refuses a share outside `(0, 1]`, a ladder whose shares sum above 1, and any share at all in a composition that has no budget policy to take a share of — all before an agent exists.
59:A bounded attempt is stopped at its own ceiling, which is what the cell has already spent plus the share of each cap: the runner arms it through [`ctx.sessionBudgets.boundAttempt`](../../guard/budget-policy/README.md#ctxsessionbudgets) for exactly that attempt and releases it before the validation. The stop records a `budget/breach` carrying `scope: 'attempt'`, which rejects the step or cancels the child without blocking the cell's goal; the runner then validates the tree that attempt left, as it does after any attempt, and moves to the next rung. The cell's own caps still end the cell, and their breach carries no scope and blocks the goal, so a cell that ran out is still a failed cell rather than a longer one.
61:The stamp records the ladder beside `model`, which stays the first attempt's route, so a fold that groups by route alone still sees where the run started while a fold that groups by the arm sees the whole escalation. Each stamped rung carries the route and the `share` its attempt was allowed, so two ladders that divide one cell budget differently are two arms. Every `EnvironmentRunAttempt` states the `model` it ran on and the `transcript` it ran under. A route implementer changes route through the model selection the runner installed on the cell agent, applied before the attempt's first step; a delegated one starts its child on the rung's model id, because a provider names its own models and the rung's harness `provider` is a fact about the route rather than an argument the provider takes.
97:2. **Arms the wall budget.** The smaller of `remainingWallMs` and the attempt's share of the wall cap becomes a deadline on the child's cancellation, one millisecond past it so the recorded span strictly exceeds the ceiling. An attempt the deadline ends records `stopReason: 'budget-deadline'`, which is what separates a budget from the seam's `aborted` that an operator's cancellation also produces. That attempt did work, so the tree it left is validated; the cell's own remaining budget then ends the run, while a rung's share ends only that attempt and the next rung runs on what the cell kept. A child a provider refuses to start because the deadline already fired leaves no delegation record; the breach is the record.
98:3. **Charges what the child spent.** `recordForeignSpend` writes one `usage/foreign` per child run — `reportedUsage` for an out-of-process child, the in-process child's summed `usage` otherwise, and `reportedCostUsd` converted at the deployment's `foreignCostEurPerUsd`. The budget fold adds it, so `maxTotalTokens` and a cost cap bound a delegated cell exactly as they bound a route cell, from the next attempt's measurement onward. A bounded attempt is measured once more right after that charge, while its own ceilings still stand, so a child that overran its rung's share records the attempt-scoped breach where it happened instead of at the next attempt.
195:- **A delegated rung's token and cost share is measured only once its child has returned** — nothing here observes what an out-of-band child spends while it runs, so a share of `maxTotalTokens` or `maxCostEur` cannot cut a delegated attempt short; the attempt-scoped breach is recorded after the charge and the next rung runs on what the cell actually has left. Only the wall share bounds such an attempt while it is running, as the deadline the child is cancelled at. A route rung's shares are enforced before every step, where the pre-step check already measures.

=== budget-policy README ===
48:- `boundAttempt(agent, share)` — bound the work about to start to a share of the caps that session runs under, and return the wall budget it may consume plus the disposer that releases the bound. See [a share of the caps](#a-share-of-the-caps).
52:A driver that divides one session between several units of work calls `boundAttempt(agent, share)` before each one. Each ceiling is the spend the session has already made plus `share` of that cap's value: the share is taken of the caps, not of what is left of them, so the slice a caller chose is the slice it gets whatever the units before it spent. The returned `wallMs` is `share` of the wall cap as a duration from the instant the bound was armed, which a driver whose work proposes no step of its own arms as a deadline; it is absent when the session runs under no wall cap, as is every ceiling when the session runs under no caps at all.
54:While the bound stands, `enforce` measures the session's own caps first and these ceilings second, so a session that has spent its whole budget reports that rather than the share of it the work in flight was allowed. A breach of a ceiling carries `scope: 'attempt'`: it appends `budget/breach` and rejects the step exactly as a cap breach does, and it leaves the goal alone, so the session continues under caps it has not spent. One bound stands per session at a time, and the disposer releases it.
76:1. Appends `budget/breach` with the cap that tripped, the measured spend, the ceiling it exceeded, and the `scope` of that ceiling. The caps are evaluated in the fixed order `maxInputTokens`, `maxOutputTokens`, `maxTotalTokens`, `maxWallMs`, `maxCostEur`, and the first one exceeded is the one recorded. A record stating no scope is the session's own caps; `scope: 'attempt'` is [a share of them](#a-share-of-the-caps).
77:2. Blocks a current `active` goal through `ctx.goals.block` with code `budget-exhausted` and the message `Session budget <cap> exceeded: <measured> of <limit>.` The block is durable and disarms continuation, so a goal-round driver does not resume the goal afterwards. A composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current goal, or whose goal already left `active` still gets the breach record and the stopped turn. An `attempt` breach skips this step: the session's own caps still hold, so its goal stays active.
92:`@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy/invariant` recomputes each durable record independently. A breach's recorded `measured` must exceed `limit` whatever its scope, and for the log-derived caps it must equal this package's fold over exactly the events preceding the record; `maxCostEur` depends on the deployment pricing table, which the log does not carry, so a cost breach is checked only for the exceeded-its-limit relation. A price must cite an earlier `assistant/message` with the same turn and step whose billed tokens and route it reproduces exactly, its `costEur` must equal its own rates applied to its own tokens, and no earlier `usage/priced` may carry the same turn and step. A `usage/foreign` must account for work no earlier record of the same log accounts for and must state no negative spend; what the implementer actually spent is outside the log, so nothing here recomputes it.
114:- **A share bounds one unit of work at a time** — `boundAttempt` replaces whatever bound stands on the session, so a driver that runs two units of work concurrently on one session cannot give each its own ceilings. The environment runner's attempts are sequential, which is the only consumer this supports.
115:- **Session-scoped only** — the caps measure one session log. A deployment that wants a per-workspace, per-user, or per-day ceiling has no aggregation point here; subagent sessions carry their own logs and their own independent budgets.
